claims.text: Standard HVOF deposition of FeCoNiCrAl using 15–45 μm feedstock produces a bond coat that is thinner than required.
The intervention is to increase the mass feed rate of the same 15–45 μm powder during HVOF spraying.
A higher powder feed rate produces a higher in-flight particle flux.
Higher particle flux increases impingement density and overlapping deposition, thereby increasing coating build-up.
Maintaining the same spray thermal and velocity conditions constrains oxidation of individual particles.
The relevant protective oxides are primarily α-Al2O3 and Cr2O3 and are confined to the coating or particle surface.
Increasing powder feed rate improves deposition efficiency because more molten or semi-molten particles reach and adhere to the substrate per unit time.
Elevated powder mass throughput reduces particle dwell time in the high-temperature spray environment.
Reduced high-temperature dwell time keeps in-flight oxidation minimal.
The increased feed rate will produce a statistically significant increase in bond-coat thickness relative to the standard-feed-rate baseline.
The coating may be 50–100% thicker than the baseline coating.
The thicker coating will retain a dense microstructure and low as-sprayed oxidation.
The intervention should remain effective in oxidizing thermal-barrier-coating service at approximately 1000–1050 °C.

The intervention remains effective when flame temperature, spray distance, substrate preheat, carrier gas, and atmosphere are otherwise held constant and overheating or longer dwell times are avoided.
An excessive feed-rate increase could disrupt particle thermal history or deposition uniformity and negate the benefit.
Prior HVOF studies support controlled particle oxidation and deposition-efficiency aspects of the proposed mechanism.
The proposed controlled experiment varies powder feed rate while holding the other HVOF variables and substrates constant.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant thickness increase, or obtaining an oxidation increase that compromises integrity, would falsify the hypothesis.
